title: Group and pair weights gave opposite signs for short-lag depth changes in deep ComCat pairs in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested signed depth change in nearby deep ComCat earthquake pairs in 2000-2025. Both events had preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth greater than 300 km. Thirteen graph groups had pairs at both seven-day and 30-365-day gaps within 200 km. The equal-group short-minus-reference depth contrast was +27.28 km, with conditional 95% group bootstrap limits of +5.56 to +50.29 km and an exact fair-sign p value of 0.0425. Positive means more downward change at short gaps. Pooled pairs gave -5.86 km, with limits of -10.40 to +39.08 km. Three later count-weight checks also gave negative but uncertain point estimates. The 100 km check was uncertain. Eight groups had one short pair, but removing them did not remove the positive equal-group estimate. Thus the sign depends on the population weights. The result does not establish vertical migration, triggering or a change between eras. Mixed magnitude methods, catalog error, selected graph groups, small group counts and revised records limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, figures, exact source hashes and a scalar audit support reproduction. External event records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Group and pair weights give opposite point-estimate signs. Conditional 95% group bootstrap intervals show uncertainty.
